markers.reading: Kenzo approaches Karawa in morning light; the attack is subsequently placed in early morning, with Delwath later calling it dawn.

evidence.quote: As you approach Karawa, the first thing you see from a distance in the morning light is a red sandstone mesa standing above the rocky desert ground.

So it's morning. It would be early enough that it's not the middle of the blazing heat. It's, but it's, it's still, I think it's still ear, you know, early spring, right? So, you know, maybe mid-April, something like that. So it's not the heat of the summer yet.
the villagers who are sort of out on their early morning errands are just scattering.
... uh, were, uh, rampaging in Karawa, Karawa at dawn this morning.

markers.note: The DM tentatively compares the season to “maybe mid-April”; no calendar day or year is spoken. This differs from the YAML March placement without settling an alternative date.

markers.reading: Delwath describes roughly a minute looking for the unseen magical disturbance while the others talk.

evidence.quote: After about, after about a few, a minute of that, or, or while you guys are talking, after... Well, you could say something at the moment.

markers.reading: Delwath completes his short rest at the teahouse while the others gear up or visit the temple; the remaining half-hour is part of the rest.

evidence.quote: I think, um, maybe we should, uh, take a short refreshment and, and, um, take a short rest, in D&D terms.

markers.note: The full rest includes prior refreshments; do not add the remaining thirty minutes again. The temple round-trip duration remains an estimate, not a separately measured interval.

markers.reading: The trackers spend an unspecified interval searching for the hyenas’ tracks around town.

evidence.quote: Um, so the two of you, um, spend some time searching around for tracks. Um, so the...

markers.reading: The party walks from Karawa through scrub desert to hard rock in about three to four hours; this refines the earlier half-day description.

evidence.quote: You, you continue for sort of maybe half a day, uh, uh, traveling through the sort of desert landscape, s- uh, sort of scrubby brush most of-
But the tracks are heading more in a northeasterly direction. It's relatively easy travel for, you know, two, three hours or so. Um,

Um, until after about three, four hours travel, um, following these tracks, uh, the, the... You sort of climb up a little bit and get to a, a stretch of hard rock. markers.reading: The party progresses into the rocky canyon lands for about an hour in all, including the earlier twenty-to-thirty-minute stretch.

evidence.quote: Um, get up very early, pre-dawn the following day to, for, to press on, um, traveling as hard and fast as you can to get to the oasis.

yamlCheck.dateAnchor: March 22–23, 1748 comes from YAML only. The transcript establishes morning, an overnight, and the following moonlit evening, but tentatively says “maybe mid-April” during opening weather description.
yamlCheck.explanation: One completed overnight supports the YAML relative span. The tentative spoken seasonal date leaves the absolute month unresolved; no definite replacement date is established.
